output.review_comment:
The new implementation does make all 9 tests pass, but it does so by adding a rule that isn't in the docstring, which the teammate explicitly said is the source of truth.

Docstring rule 2 states small words are lowercased "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`" — only two exceptions. The PR adds a third, undocumented exception: `is_after_colon = words[index - 1].endswith(':')`, which capitalizes a small word whenever the previous word ends in a colon. This is exactly what makes `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass (`"field: a year"` → `"Field: A Year"`), but per the literal docstring text that "a" is neither the first nor last word of the whole string, so it should stay lowercase. The docstring was never updated to mention colons at all, so the code and its own documentation now disagree — a future reader/maintainer following the docstring would implement this differently and reintroduce the failing test.

This looks like logic added specifically to satisfy one test case rather than a faithful reading of the documented contract. Given the instructions ("docstrings are the source of truth," "don't change the tests"), the right move here was either:
1. Recognize the docstring and test are in conflict and flag that back to the teammate instead of silently resolving it, or
2. If the after-colon behavior is indeed intended, update the docstring to state that rule explicitly so the code's contract matches its behavior.

As written, please update the docstring to accurately describe the "word following a colon-ending word is treated like a first word" rule (or otherwise resolve the conflict), so the documented contract and implementation agree. Once that's done I'm happy to approve — the rest of the logic (rule 1 mixed-case preservation, rule 3 default capitalization) looks correct and matches the docstring.
